parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, no npm dependencies, no forbidden Map usage, exact bidict formatting, duplicate-key and duplicate-value behavior, copy independence, inverse lookup, and the executable as behavioral oracle.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed behavior, then split implementation into four child-owned files: pyrepr, bidict, argparse, and test19 entry. The parent retained integration and final verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Child code created a lib directory, exported repr helpers, implemented Bidict with key de-duplication and duplicate-value errors, implemented parseArgs with full usage text, and wrote an entry file importing the modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All child files were present under /output, the parent ran integrated node-vs-executable comparisons, read the final files, and delivered test19.mjs plus lib modules as the artifact.
parallel.verification: Verification covered the four samples plus duplicate key, duplicate value, v1=999, missing argument, invalid int, and negative/zero integer cases, but the checks hid stderr and the parent accepted known stderr and parser-token caveats.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official result still failed 12 cases; the visible unresolved gaps are simplified exception stderr and an argparse edge where an option token after a value flag is consumed instead of rejected like argparse.

serial.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs output, manual parsing, bidict representation, copy behavior, inverse lookup, and sample output formatting, but treated error behavior and duplicate-value handling less completely.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent owned the whole migration, planned top-level bidict, pyformat, argparse, and test19 files, and wrote them in one step without child handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial code wrote a Bidict class and inverse view, a repr helper, an argparse helper, and an entry script; however Bidict.set overwrote or appended without checking duplicate values and usage errors were simplified.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The four top-level .mjs files were mutually imported and artifact validation found test19.mjs plus its support files, with no cross-agent merge or handoff boundary.
serial.verification: The serial run compared the four sample cases and one negative integer case against the executable, but did not test duplicate-value failures or detailed argparse/error stderr.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official result failed 14 cases; visible issues include missing bidict value-duplication enforcement, incomplete argparse usage text, first-missing-only missing-arg reporting, and simplified exception behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full prompt and additionally probed duplicate-key, duplicate-value, v1=999, missing-arg, invalid-int, and negative-int behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the prompt and two sample outputs but did not probe duplicate-value behavior before writing code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader task-knowledge coverage and implemented duplicate-value checks; serial missed that requirement, while both left some error-output details incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by file and assigned pyrepr, bidict, argparse, and test19 to separate child agents with the parent owning final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all design and implementation ownership in the main agent and wrote every module directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child handoff and acceptance boundaries; serial avoided coordination overhead but relied on one actor's implementation choices.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied explicit shared exports and import paths for all child-owned files, but also carried known unresolved error/parser caveats into final acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface transfer; interfaces were internal to its own top-level files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel module interfaces were mostly coherent, but the parent-level acceptance boundary left cross-file behavior gaps unresolved; serial's gaps were ordinary direct implementation defects.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child code used lib/ modules and implemented duplicate-value rejection in Bidict plus full usage text in parseArgs, with concise custom stderr for bidict errors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote top-level modules and an entry file, but its Bidict.set never rejected duplicate values and its usage line was only `usage: test19.mjs [-h]`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's bidict semantics were closer to the executable, which likely accounts for the two-case score edge; serial's direct code omitted key hidden behaviors.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned, the parent received the aggregate swarm result, then read the child-produced files before closing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results; the main agent's writes were immediately local to the same actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no missing join in parallel, but the parent accepted the joined result while known caveats remained; serial had no analogous result-lifecycle boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct files under /output/lib plus the entry file; the parent later exercised the assembled artifact and artifact validation captured those files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote four top-level files and verified the assembled entry directly, with no live multi-agent shared-state contention.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete write collision appears in parallel; the main difference is directory/interface organization and subsequent acceptance, not a shared-state overwrite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran sample and edge stdout/exit-code comparisons, but redirected stderr in those diffs and closed while identifying stderr and parser-token deviations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran four sample diffs and a negative-integer diff, then declared character-for-character success without testing duplicate-value or detailed argparse failure behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verified more cases than serial but still treated known mismatch classes as acceptable; serial had narrower verification and missed duplicate-value failures entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and 496.667 agent seconds but completed without timeout before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main agent, 127.444 agent seconds, and completed without timeout before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent substantially more time and tokens, but no evidence shows deadline exhaustion; both closed voluntarily and both failed official evaluation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official records make this a both-fail pair, not a discordant outcome: parallel passed 145 of 157 tests and serial passed 143 of 157. Parallel solved more bidict semantics by probing and delegating a Bidict implementation with duplicate-value checks, while serial's single-agent Bidict never rejects duplicate values. Both attempts still left hidden acceptance gaps, especially around exact stderr/argparse behavior; the retained parallel pattern is adverse within the parallel process but does not explain a pass/fail split because both failed.
parallel_contributors: Parallel subagents produced a more complete Bidict implementation, including duplicate-value rejection and duplicate-key last-value behavior.
Parallel parent closed despite known remaining stderr and parser-edge caveats after limited integrated checks.
serial_contributors: Serial wrote a direct Bidict implementation whose set/constructor path never checks duplicate values.
Serial argparse handling used a simplified usage line and only first-missing reporting, leaving more hidden CLI behavior uncovered.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's missing duplicate-value enforcement is an ordinary coding omission in the single-agent implementation.
Both runs simplified exception stderr compared with the executable traceback, so that issue is not a proven parallel-only root cause.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official pass counts are available in the mounted pair, so individual hidden testcase attributions remain inferential.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors in a both-fail pair, not an exclusive root cause
